syllabusTopics: Hydrogen: chemistry of atomic and nascent hydrogen; isotopes of hydrogen and their uses
Application of hydrogen as fuel; heavy water and its applications
Allotropes of oxygen: definition of allotropy and examples; oxygen — types of oxides (acidic, basic, neutral, amphoteric, peroxide and mixed oxides)
Applications of hydrogen peroxide; medical and industrial application of oxygen
Ozone: occurrence, preparation of ozone from oxygen, structure of ozone, test for ozone, uses of ozone
Ozone layer depletion: causes, effects and control measures
Nitrogen: reason for inertness of nitrogen and active nitrogen
Chemical properties of ammonia (action with CuSO4 solution, water, FeCl3 solution, conc. HCl, mercurous nitrate paper, O2); applications and harmful effects of ammonia
Chemical properties of nitric acid: HNO3 as an acid and oxidizing agent (action with zinc, magnesium, iron, copper, sulphur, carbon, SO2 and H2S); ring test for nitrate ion
Halogens: general characteristics of halogens; comparative study on preparation, chemical properties (with water, alkali, ammonia, oxidizing character, bleaching action) and uses of Cl2, Br2 and I2
Test for Cl2, Br2 and I2

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Hydrogen's applied chapter has two stars. As a **fuel**, H₂ outranks every chemical energy carrier per gram (~142 kJ/g, three times petrol) and burns to nothing but water — in the oxy-hydrogen flame at ~2800 °C, in rocket tanks as cryogenic liquid, and most elegantly in the **fuel cell**, where anode H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ and cathode ½O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂O deliver electricity at 60–70 % efficiency with steam the only…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, ΔH = −286 kJ/mol - Anode: H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻; Cathode: ½O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂O - CH₄ + H₂O → CO + 3H₂ (steam reforming, current H₂ source) - D₂O: mp 3.8 °C, bp 101.4 °C, d = 1.108 g/mL

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Heavy water (D2O) is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors because it slows neutrons efficiently while absorbing very few of them."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The rocket tank*** — liquid hydrogen plus liquid oxygen lifts every heavy launcher: highest specific energy in a tank, and the exhaust is a cloud of steam.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Hydrogen as Fuel and the Water That Is Not Two applied faces of hydrogen: **D₂O (heavy water)** with its nuclear-reactor career, and **hydrogen as the fuel of the future** — the only combustion product of which is water. This topic covers hydrogen fuel's chemistry, its storage problem, and heavy water's preparation and applications.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Hydrogen as a fuel - **Combustion:** 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, ΔH = −286 kJ/mol — the highest energy per unit mass of any chemical fuel (~142 kJ/g vs petrol ~48 kJ/g). - **Zero-carbon:** the only product is water — no CO₂, CO, SO₂ or particulates.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 142 kJ/g, 3x petrol, product = water only. Fuel cell: anode H2 -> 2H+ + 2e-, cathode O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> H2O. D2O numbers: 3.8 / 101.4 / 1.108 / 99.75%. Moderator slows, control rods absorb.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The isotope effect is the engine of heavy-water production: identical chemistry, different bond-breaking speeds — electrolysis separates what chemistry cannot.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Hydrogen fuel: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, dH = -286 kJ/mol, ~142 kJ/g (3x petrol), only product water. Uses: oxy-hydrogen flame ~2800 C, fuel cells (anode H2 -> 2H+ + 2e-, cathode 1/2O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> H2O, ~60-70% efficient), rocket propellant.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Fuel-cell buses and taxis already run in several countries; the same reaction 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O that powers them is the one every electrolysis plant runs backwards.

rows.text: List the three hydrogen storage strategies with one drawback each.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Heavy water is not "more purified water":** D₂O is chemically H₂O with deuterium in place of protium — a different isotope, not a different purity.  ·  **Fuel cells do not burn hydrogen:** they electrochemically combine it — no flame, higher efficiency; calling a fuel cell "hydrogen combustion" loses the point.
